findings.description: The new lookup interpolates the caller-supplied model string directly into bash array subscripts (`${MODEL_IDS[$1]:-$1}`, `${MODEL_PROVIDERS[$1]:-${MODEL_PROVIDERS[$id]:-}}`) after sourcing `generated-model-maps.sh`. Plain `${arr[key]}` expansion is injection-safe only for arrays declared with `declare -A`. If the generated file omits either name (for example no aliases emitted) or declares it indexed, bash treats the reference as an indexed array and evaluates the subscript arithmetically, so a model id like `x[$(cmd)]` executes `cmd`. The subshell discards stderr (`2>/dev/null`) and swallows source failures (`|| exit 0`), so nothing would surface. Model ids reach this path from `.loa.config.yaml` stage/model settings via `routes_to_agy` and the new `*)` branch of `provider_of` in `run-preflight.sh`. The code checks `-f "$maps"` and the bash version but never verifies the declared type of the arrays or the shape of the id.
findings.failure_mode: A repo-controlled or malformed model id reaches an arithmetic subscript context during preflight or gate checks and runs shell commands whenever the generated maps file does not declare both MODEL_IDS and MODEL_PROVIDERS as associative arrays.
findings.suggested_fix: Validate the id before any lookup, e.g. `[[ $m =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:/-]*$ ]] || return 0`, and inside the subshell assert that `declare -p MODEL_IDS` and `declare -p MODEL_PROVIDERS` both begin with `declare -A` before dereferencing (exit the subshell otherwise). Add a bats case feeding a hostile id (`'x[$(touch /tmp/pwn)]'`) against a maps file that lacks MODEL_IDS and assert nothing runs.

findings.cross_file_justification: The bash predicate is documented as the twin of `loa_cheval.config.loader.routes_to_agy` / `cheval._entry_routes_to_agy`, and `test_agy_opt_in_gate.py::test_routes_to_agy_matches_the_bash_rule` now asserts `deep-research-pro` and `researcher` are agy-routed under cli-only. When the bash side cannot read the maps it silently gives the opposite answer for exactly those ids.
findings.description: `agy_catalog_provider` falls back silently to the legacy `gemini*` name rule when `generated-model-maps.sh` is absent, fails to source, or bash is older than 4. Under `cli-only`, `routes_to_agy deep-research-pro` then returns 1 (not agy-routed) and `agy_route_planned` reports the route as planned even with `hounfour.headless.agy_opt_in` off, while cheval classifies the same hop as agy-routed and refuses it. This recreates the bash-versus-Python split that R3 set out to close, in the direction where preflight is more permissive than the runtime gate, and no warning is emitted.
findings.failure_mode: Preflight reports a Google catalog model as planned without the opt-in and cheval refuses it at runtime; the argv-exposure route is never flagged by preflight for those ids when the maps are unreadable.
findings.suggested_fix: When bash is 4 or newer and the maps file is missing or unsourceable, print a one-time warning to stderr and return a distinct status (e.g. 2) from `agy_catalog_provider` so `routes_to_agy` and `agy_route_planned` can report 'unresolvable' rather than 'planned'. Add a bats test that removes the maps file and asserts the warning and the non-planned result.

findings.description: The live-spend guard switched from a before/after comparison of the real host ledger `.run/model-invoke.jsonl` to checking only the file named by `LOA_MODELINV_LOG_PATH`. The new check is only as strong as every cheval invoke path honoring that variable; a path that still appends to the default ledger would now escape detection. The fixture also raises KeyError (a test error, not a clean assertion) if the `_isolate_ledgers` conftest fixture does not export the variable, and the module relies on `os` being imported, which the shown diff does not add. This guard exists to stop test payloads from being sent to a real provider.
findings.failure_mode: A live model call that escapes the fake in this module is no longer detected if cheval records it anywhere other than the tmp ledger, so test content could reach a real provider silently.
findings.suggested_fix: At fixture setup assert `LOA_MODELINV_LOG_PATH` is set and resolves under tmp_path, and assert via cheval's own ledger-path resolver that it will write there. Optionally retain a module-scoped size-delta check on the host ledger as a secondary signal with a message that names concurrent runs as a possible cause.
